causeCollection.description:
A lower-level set of structured errors.

causeIndexedCollection.description:
A lower-level set of structured errors.
Each of these errors MUST have index set.

Only oneOf `causeWrapped`, `causeSimple`, `causeCollection`, or `causeIndexedCollection` will ever be set.

causeIsInternal.description: If true, then the cause (`causeWrapped`, `causeSimple`, `causeCollection`, or `causeIndexedCollection`) should be hidden from the user.

causeSimple.description:
Simple string error type.

Only oneOf `causeWrapped`, `causeSimple`, `causeCollection`, or `causeIndexedCollection` will ever be set.

domain.description:
The "domain" for the error.  If empty, it is an EDA
core error.  Alternatively it can be an EDA application
"apiVersion" value (e.g. interfaces.eda.nokia.com/v1alpha1)
indicating that the error is specific to that application.
The domain gives the receiver information that they can use
to help them interpret the "type" field.

index.description:
When processing an array, errors may be generated related to a particular array item.
If set, this index indicates to which array item the error applies.

message.description: The basic text error message for the error response.

ref.description: Reference to the error source. Should typically be the URI of the request.

type.description:
Type defines a unique identifier for the error, within the domain.
This may be used (along with the domain) to find an internationalization translation for the message.

SHOULD be a valid golang identifier, and SHOULD be in UpperCamelCase.

values.description:
Associated data/information.
The error "message" may contain {{name}} escapes that should be substituted with information from this dictionary.

Note that this map MUST NOT contain JSON objects (`{...}`) or arrays (`[...]`), only simple JSON types are permitted.

the target JSON object that should be moved to the location specified by the "path"
field.

op.description: The type of operation this patch should perform.

path.description:
The path to the field within the target JSON object
that should be patched according to the "op" field.

value.description:
This field would be set to the value which the user intends to put in the
field referenced by the "path" field.  The type of the value should match
the type of the field as indicated by the schema of the resource being
patched.

x-permissive.description:
For an "add" operation, an already-present field referenced by the "path" will
result in an error unless this field is true.  Similarly for a non-existent
target field of a "remove" operation.

spec.description: RebootSpec defines the desired state of Reboot

drains.description: Configure drains to gracefully drain traffic away from nodes before rebooting.

skip.description: Do not run any drain operations. Nodes will be rebooted without attempting to gracefully drain them.
skip.title: Skip Drains

waitSeconds.description:
Seconds to wait before rebooting a node after the drain has been initiated.
This is used to allow time for any traffic to drain away from the node before reboot.
waitSeconds.title: Wait Time

drains.title: Drains

nodeSelectors.description:
List of node selectors to select nodes to reboot.
This matches labels on TopoNode resources, including those TopoNodes in the list of nodes that will be rebooted.
If no nodes are specified, and no node selectors are specified, all nodes in the given namespace will be selected.
This is a list of label expressions, e.g. ["eda.nokia.com/role=leaf"].
nodeSelectors.title: Node Selectors

ui-conditions.errorMsg: Nodes, Node Selectors or Tranches must be set
Nodes, Node Selectors or Tranches must be set

options.description: Reboot Options to configure how the reboot is performed.

componentRecoveryTimeoutSeconds.description:
Seconds to wait for ControlModule and InterfaceModule recovery after ReconnectionTimeout.
Minimum value is 60 seconds (1 minute), maximum value is 3600 seconds (1 hour).
The default value is 900 seconds (15 minutes).
componentRecoveryTimeoutSeconds.title: ComponentRecoveryTimeout

delaySeconds.description:
Delay in seconds before performing the reboot.
Minimum value is 0 seconds (immediate), maximum value is 300 seconds (5 minutes).
delaySeconds.title: Delay (seconds)

force.description:
Force the reboot, bypassing any softchecks on the node.
For example: unsaved configuration between running and startup config.
force.title: Force

ignoreInterfaceModuleRecover.description: Do not require InterfaceModules to transition to Up After Reboot.
ignoreInterfaceModuleRecover.title: Ignore InterfaceModule recovery

message.description: Supply a broadcast message to all users logged in to the node(s) being rebooted.
message.title: Node Reboot Message

rebootMethod.description: Reboot method to use, currently only cold reboot is supported, other methods may be added in the future.
rebootMethod.title: Reboot Method

reconnectionTimeoutSeconds.description:
Seconds to wait for node to come back online after reboot.
Minimum value is 60 seconds (1 minute), maximum value is 3600 seconds (1 hour).
The default value is 600 seconds (10 minutes).
SR OS nodes in NPP maintenance mode use 1800 seconds when unset or set to default value of 600 seconds.
reconnectionTimeoutSeconds.title: ReconnectionTimeout

options.title: Options

prompts.description:
Control when to prompt the user for input.
If any pre or post checks fail, the user will be prompted for input, but this may be used to prompt even if they're successful.

Prompts the user to confirm wether to proceed with the reboot or wait for nodes to recover.
InputSafety prompts the user for confirmation to proceed if any unintended input is detected.
RecoveryTimeout prompts the user for confirmation, to wait for an additional ReconnectionTimeoutSeconds duration, allowing time for the node to recover.
prompts.title: When to prompt

skip.description: Skip all user prompts and execute without any user interaction.
skip.title: Skip Prompts

prompts.title: Prompts

tranches.description:
List of tranches to use to reboot nodes.
A tranche is a list of node selectors, and a name.
Tranches are rebooted in order, sequentially.
Tranches are rebooted before any Nodes and/or Node Selectors are evaluated. When there is overlap between a Tranche and the list of Nodes evaluated by Nodes and/or Node Selectors, the matching Node will be purged from the list of Nodes / NodeSelectors.

name.description:
Name of the tranche.
This is used to identify the tranche in the UI and in logs.
name.title: Name

nodeSelectors.description:
Node Selectors is a list of node selectors to select nodes to reboot in this tranche.
This matches labels on TopoNode resources, including those TopoNodes in the list of nodes that will be rebooted.
This is a list of label expressions, e.g. ["eda.nokia.com/role=leaf"].
nodeSelectors.title: Node Selectors

tranches.title: Tranches

rebootTime.description:
The time when the node was rebooted.

Result is the overall result of the reboot operation.
It can be one of the following values:
